quotes.quote: PSIRT Maturity Levels to demonstrate Operational Capability and Maturity
Maturity Level 1 (Basic) - The Beginning is a very fine place to start
a high-level overview of the services that a Product Security Incident Response Team might select
It may evolve over time as the mission or needs change and as the experience of the team grows.
These referenced use cases cover a spectrum of developmental levels from a newly-established PSIRT
the team shifts from reactive operations to a more proactive mode of operating, reflecting greater maturity of their processes
in this document is intended to describe a profile of a product security team
In the PSIRT Services Framework, we have a concept of Operational Foundations.
The PSIRT is best served beginning with documenting their key stakeholders.
publish your e-mail address) when they find a security issue
it is also recommended to provide pgp key to receive vulnerability reports
Vulnerability intake and triage commence the case management function of a PSIRT.
Ideally you should use the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS), but you can also use your own.
choose your yardstick and then measure all things against it
If you do not use CVSS then you must have a good explanation for customers
Maturity Level 2 (Intermediate) - I am reactive, but I’ve trained for it!
Overall, we view PSIRTs in this middle-stage of maturity as internally-focused.
It is expected that all previous services have been put into place and vetted.
you should revisit Maturity Level #1 and apply those practices
you should have successfully implemented everything from the Operational Foundations to some degree
these key things MUST be in place to ensure ongoing successful operations
the PSIRT should consider having a quantifiable process for evaluating these incoming reports (sometimes referred to as a “Bug Bar”)
The operating model you designed your processes and team around (Centralized, Distributed, Hybrid) will impact who is conducting vulnerability triage
It’s important to test out these flaws in an isolated place (to avoid ruining everyone’s day on the network).
This has been the secret sauce that sets you apart from beginning PSIRTs: experience and reflection.
Maturity Level 3 (Advanced) - Proactive...we’re ready for anything (mostly)
To get to this level it is understood that your process for ingestion, analysis, and delivery of security updates for your products is well-understood
PSIRTs operating at this level are exemplified by proactive and consistent behaviors.
To consider yourself mature, all of these processes and services need to be long-established.
They may get priority flagging and get moved straight into the analysis phase, bypassing remedial triage steps that unproven reporters may still have to hurdle.
Ideally by this stage, with repeatedly fixing previous issues, the PSIRT and all stakeholder participants are now able to deliver updates consistently.
Beyond “Level 3”
What? …. Sounds Impossible…. but it is NOT!
For a complete list of supporting resources and glossary refer to the PSIRT Services Framework
PSIRTs should have a defined charter that describes what the PSIRT does, and its scope.
Security vulnerabilities must be triaged within [#] days of receiving a report

Identify stakeholders
Establish budget
Establish policies
Establish PSIRT email address with PGP key
Establish a product registry with dependency mapping
Develop internal vulnerability reproduction capability
